name: Hours portal (tabbed front door for all hours work)
purpose: One page with seven tabs that holds everything about time: my timesheet, assignments, the approval queue, who is on the clock, history, time off and availability.

elements.name: My time
elements.does: Own timesheet and missed-clock-out fixer (MyHoursPanel).

elements.name: Assignments
elements.does: Work given to me; managers see what they gave out.

elements.name: Approvals
elements.does: Approver queue. Gated to admin, developer, tech_support.

elements.name: Field team
elements.does: Who is on the clock. admin and tech_support only.

elements.name: History
elements.does: Audit trail of every hours change, with restore of deleted entries.

elements.name: Time off
elements.does: Request leave, see balance, approve queue for managers.

elements.name: Availability
elements.does: Crew, equipment and vehicles for one day.

behaviours: Default tab is Approvals for approvers, Availability for equipment_manager, otherwise My time.
The old routes /admin/my-hours, /admin/hours-approval, /admin/team, /admin/time-off and /admin/availability are redirect stubs into this page.
problems: Seven unrelated jobs under one tab strip: a crew member wants two of them (clock and my time), an approver wants three. Assignments and Availability are scheduling, not hours.
ApprovalsTab is 1,819 lines and MyHoursPanel 1,220 lines: each mixes a dozen features (see their own entries).
rebuild: Three surfaces by job, not by data table: Clock (crew, phone-first, one screen), Timesheet (crew week view), Review (approver queue by person). Scheduling tabs move to the schedule area.
add: Per-crew-member week view for the party chief (approve own crew's time before it reaches the office).
nationwide: Roles are hard-coded role names (admin/tech_support). Week is assumed Monday to Sunday (ApprovalsTab pay-week lock). Must become per-firm: pay period type (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly), week start day, timezone.

name: Clock in / clock out (top-bar pill, hub tile, modals)
purpose: Start and stop a shift from anywhere in the admin app. Clock-out turns the elapsed time into timesheet rows.

elements.name: Clock in modal
elements.does: Optional job (job search) and activity tags; stamps started_at.

elements.name: Clock out modal
elements.does: Shows hours worked and span; per-job hour split; lunch minutes (segmented plus other); notes; tags pre-selected from clock-in.

elements.name: Long-day warning
elements.does: Message when worked > 14h: check for a missed clock-out.

behaviours: The running clock lives in browser localStorage (key starr-clock-session) and is mirrored best-effort to the server (active_clock_sessions, one row per user).
Pill and hub tile sync through a same-tab event so one clock-out cannot be logged twice.
Clock-out checks the server session first; if the server says it is gone it asks whether to log the hours anyway.
Lunch is recorded, never deducted (seed 650); the approver sees it and decides.
Only roles in CLOCKABLE_ROLES see the pill.
problems: The clock is a client-side convenience, not a record: start and end timestamps are NOT stored on the timesheet row. daily_time_logs holds only a date and a decimal hours figure, so punch times cannot be audited later (a wage-and-hour record normally needs them).
Device-local truth: clearing site data or using a second device is handled by patches (hydrate, serverStillClockedIn) rather than the server being the source of truth.
No break/meal compliance: lunch is a note only, so meal-break rules cannot be enforced or deducted.
A multi-day shift is split by local day in the browser (splitByLocalDay) using the device timezone.
No geofence or GPS stamp on clock-in even though location pings and job geofences exist elsewhere in the platform.
rebuild: Server-owned punch: a time_punches table (user, start_at, end_at, job, task, source, device, optional lat/lon, edited_by) with one open punch per user enforced by a partial unique index. The pill is a thin client. Breaks are punches too, with a per-state meal-break policy that can auto-deduct or prompt.
add: Break and meal tracking with state rules
Geofence prompt on arrival at a job site
Edit with reason and approval, never silent
Kiosk or crew-lead clocks the whole crew in
nationwide: Role list is Starr-shaped (drawer, researcher). Long-day threshold 14h is fixed. Meal-break and rest rules vary by state (CA, OR, WA, NY etc.) and need a per-state policy.
plans: docs/planning/completed/02_CLOCK_IN_WORK_MODE_2026-06-24.md (Work Mode retired; server-persisted session was a deferred idea, now partly built)

name: Clock session API (server mirror of the running clock)
purpose: Lets the server know who is on the clock so reminders and the AI assistant can see it.

elements.name: GET
elements.does: Returns the caller's open session or null; any error returns null.

elements.name: POST
elements.does: Upsert started_at, job_id, tag_ids, source.

elements.name: DELETE
elements.does: Closes the session.

behaviours: Table active_clock_sessions has user_email as primary key: one open clock per person.
No role check beyond being signed in.
problems: Only the 6pm reminder cron and the AI tool read this table. The Field team page and the team drill-down read a different table (job_time_entries), so who-is-on-the-clock is split in two (see people.field-team-tab).
Client supplies started_at, so a client can backdate its own clock with no audit.
rebuild: Fold into the server-owned punch model: the open punch IS the clock session. Timestamps are server-set; edits are separate audited corrections.
nationwide: Single timezone is not stored here; fine. Needs org_id scoping for multi-firm.

name: Offline-safe clock-out queue
purpose: A clock-out made with no signal is saved on the device and sent when the connection returns.

elements.name: Queue in localStorage
elements.does: Written first, then POSTed; retried on online, tab visible, every minute.

elements.name: client_submission_id
elements.does: Unique index in seeds/664 makes a retry return the first row instead of a duplicate.

elements.name: needsAttention state
elements.does: Server refusals (closed pay week, over 24h) are kept and shown on My time with the reason.

behaviours: buildClockOutEntries splits a multi-day shift by local day or by per-job hour allocations.
Adds a missed-clock-out warning to the notes when one shift exceeds the long-shift limit.
work_type is always written as 'general' from the clock.
problems: Good idea, but it exists because the clock is client-side. With server punches and an offline punch buffer (same idea, smaller) most of this goes away.
Clock-out always writes work_type 'general', so the pay rate/activity must be fixed by an approver afterwards.
rebuild: Keep the pattern (write locally, send with idempotency key) but queue punch events, not finished timesheet rows.
add: Service-worker background sync for field crews with no signal
nationwide: Local-day split uses device timezone; firm timezone should be configurable.

name: My time (employee timesheet)
purpose: Employee enters or edits a day's hours per job and activity, sees status, rejection reasons and the week's approved and pending pay.

elements.name: Entry rows
elements.does: Date, job (search), activity (priced menu), hours, description, notes, lunch.

elements.name: Week summary
elements.does: Total, approved, pending, rejected hours; approved pay; hours awaiting a rate.

elements.name: Day/week/month/year totals
elements.does: Review by period (S3 of the payroll plan).

elements.name: Resubmit / dispute
elements.does: Pending and rejected rows are editable; approved/adjusted/disputed are admin-only.

behaviours: Rows saved via POST /api/admin/time-logs; replaced rows pass replace_ids.
Locked pay periods return HTTP 423 and the UI says why.
Priced from the one pay model, so the figure shown equals what the approver sees.
problems: Two ways to enter the same day: the clock, and typing hours here. Both write the same table, but only the clock gives a hint of when work happened.
Hours are free text numbers (max 24, no start/end), so overlaps between jobs on one day cannot be detected.
Employee picks a pay activity (work_type) on their own timesheet; the pay model is exposed to the person being paid, which most firms keep with the office.
1,220-line component: week summary, entry editor, history, pending-queue notice and locks all in one.
rebuild: Week grid (days by jobs) fed by punches. Manual entry is a fallback marked 'manual' and may need a reason. Pay activity picks are limited to what the firm allows employees to choose.
add: Crew-lead entry for the whole crew
Employee acknowledgement/attestation at period end (required in some states)
nationwide: Activity names and pay menu are Starr-seeded. Week start fixed. Needs configurable job-cost codes and attestation text.
plans: docs/planning/pending/PAYROLL_HOURS_AND_EMPLOYEE_MONEY_2026-08-12.md (S3 shipped; period close shipped as a lock)

name: Hours approvals (review queue)
purpose: The approver reads submitted timesheets by person, approves, rejects (reason required), adjusts hours and pay, locks the week and starts the payout.

elements.name: People list
elements.does: Employees with pending hours first, most recently clocked on top, with logged/approved/paid stats.

elements.name: Flags
elements.does: duplicate, long_day (>14h), high_total (>60h), needs_review, late entry after lock.

elements.name: Bulk approve / reject
elements.does: Selected ids via POST /api/admin/time-logs/approve; bulk approve warns on duplicates.

elements.name: Mark paid / unpaid
elements.does: Bulk or single, stamps paid_at/paid_by without touching approver fields.

elements.name: Lock / unlock week
elements.does: Writes pay_period_locks; a close snapshot is taken (seed 587).

elements.name: Prepare payout
elements.does: On close, creates a draft payout batch for the week.

elements.name: Add hours for someone
elements.does: Office entry on behalf of an employee (entered_by recorded), auto-approved.

elements.name: Advances and bonuses
elements.does: Advance and bonus forms live in this same tab.

behaviours: Approve, reject, adjust each write an audit stamp and notify the employee (bell and push).
Adjust opens PayDecisionModal to set pay as well as hours.
Approvers are notified on submission, with per-admin opt-out.
problems: 1,819 lines doing six jobs: review, payroll close, payout start, advances, bonuses, office data entry.
Approval is by single approver with role admin; no party-chief first-level approval, no two-step (crew lead then office).
Approver sees punch-free rows so 'long day' is the only missed-clock-out signal.
Week is the only period shape; the lock must exactly match a Monday-Sunday row (earlier bug, comments at line 131).
Approving does not check overtime or state rules; overtime is only computed by the legacy payroll engine.
rebuild: Review screen only: person list, week grid, flags, approve/reject/adjust. Period close is a separate 'Close pay period' wizard that shows regular, overtime, PTO and totals per person by state rules, then hands to payroll export. Advances and bonuses move to the pay area.
add: Overtime and double-time preview per person before approving
nationwide: APPROVERS role list hard-coded. Long-day 14h and high-total 60h thresholds are fixed. Overtime thresholds should come from the work state.

name: Pay decision (price a day at several rates)
purpose: The approver splits a day across activity rates (for example 2h drawing, 6h field) or types a custom amount, with notes.

elements.name: Base pay banner
elements.does: The employee's agreed base pay is always shown.

elements.name: Activity lines
elements.does: Hours per activity, priced from the pay menu.

elements.name: Custom amount
elements.does: Overrides rules; revision history kept; employee is notified.

behaviours: Stored in time_log_pay_decisions with revisions (seed 574).
Approved hours with no price are 'undecided' and pay zero until priced.
problems: Two places hold pay for one entry: daily_time_logs.total_pay (stamped at submit) and time_log_pay_decisions. All readers must prefer the decision; one mistake yields two numbers.
Pay is per-day dollars, not per-hour rate by class, which makes overtime and prevailing-wage reporting hard.
rebuild: Store hours split by pay class (regular, OT, DT, PTO, prevailing, per-diem) on the entry. A decision edits classes and rates, not a dollar total.
nationwide: Needs prevailing wage (Davis-Bacon, state) and job-class rates; none exist.

name: Office logs hours for an employee
purpose: Record a crew member's day when they forgot or have no phone, setting hours and pay.

elements.name: Whose hours picker
elements.does: Required; a typo'd address is rejected.

elements.name: entered_by column
elements.does: Marks rows the office typed, kept NULL for self-submitted.

behaviours: Fails closed: naming another person without admin returns 403.
Auto-approved and the employee gets a notification (hours-entered-for-you).
problems: Hidden inside the approvals tab form rather than being a first-class 'add time' action.
Only admin can do it; a party chief cannot enter for their crew.
rebuild: Same endpoint, exposed as 'Add time for...' in both the week grid and the person card, allowed for crew leads for their own crew, always flagged and visible to the employee.
add: Employee confirm or dispute of office-entered time
nationwide: Role names to configurable permissions.

name: Time logs API group
purpose: The only write path for hours: submit, edit, delete, approve, reject, adjust, dispute, bulk approve, mark paid, lock, price.

elements.name: GET
elements.does: Employees see own, admins see all with filters (dates must be YYYY-MM-DD).

elements.name: POST
elements.does: Insert entries; rejects hours over 24 per day; HTTP 423 in locked periods; skips duplicates; optional user_email for admins.

elements.name: PUT
elements.does: Employee may edit pending and rejected; admin approve, reject, adjust, dispute.

elements.name: DELETE
elements.does: Pending or rejected only for employees; admin any (restorable via history).

elements.name: approve (POST)
elements.does: Bulk approve, reject, mark_paid, mark_unpaid.

behaviours: Status set: pending, approved, rejected, disputed, adjusted (CHECK constraint).
Rate is stamped on the row at submit from the pay model (resolve-rate).
A database trigger (seed 664) writes the audit history for every change.
problems: Authorisation is isAdmin only; no finer 'can approve hours' or 'can see wages' permission (finance role exists but is not used here).
867-line route file mixes validation, pricing, notification fan-out and duplicate rules.
Database CHECK hours > 0 and <= 24 and numeric(5,2): no punch times, no negative corrections.
No unique key per person, day and job, relying on a code-level duplicate check.
rebuild: Split into punches (raw time), timesheet periods (submit/approve per period) and pay lines (computed, never hand-stamped). Keep the audit trigger and the idempotency key; they are the good parts.
nationwide: Role gating by name; org scoping is through supabaseAdmin (service role), not row security. Pay stamped from one firm's rate model.

name: Pay period lock and close snapshot
purpose: Freezes employee edits for a date range and records what the period held when it was closed.

elements.name: Lock / unlock
elements.does: Row per period; employee edits give 423.

elements.name: Late-entry marker
elements.does: Flags entries dated inside a closed period but arriving after.

behaviours: Helpers treat a missing table or error as unlocked (best effort).
Admins can still adjust inside a lock.
problems: Lock is date-range only; it computes and sends nothing. 'Close' does not produce an overtime-aware total.
Fails open: a query error means the period is treated as unlocked.
rebuild: Make the period a first-class record (type, start, end, state: open, submitted, approved, exported, paid) that drives the timesheet submit/approve/export workflow. Fail closed.
nationwide: Pay frequency (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, monthly) is not modelled; weekly Monday start is implicit.
plans: docs/planning/pending/PAYROLL_HOURS_AND_EMPLOYEE_MONEY_2026-08-12.md (period close shipped as lock plus snapshot, seed 587)

name: Hours history and audit trail
purpose: Show who posted, reviewed, edited or deleted every hours entry and let an admin restore a deleted row.

elements.name: Event list
elements.does: Fed by a database trigger so out-of-app writes show too.

elements.name: Restore
elements.does: Puts a deleted row back exactly as it was.

behaviours: Employees see their own; admins see everyone.
problems: Hours history and the generic Audit Log are two audit viewers.
No export for a wage dispute.
rebuild: Keep. Embed in the person record and in each timesheet row ('history' drawer) and offer CSV/PDF export.
nationwide: Retention period per state (typically 3 to 7 years) is not configurable.

name: Field team (who is on the clock)
purpose: Dispatcher view: each active employee, clock state, last ping, and a button to nudge them to log hours.

elements.name: Employee rows
elements.does: Clock state, duration, last reminder.

elements.name: Send ping
elements.does: Notification asking the person to log hours.

behaviours: Clock state is read from job_time_entries where end_time is null.
problems: Clock-in writes to active_clock_sessions and daily_time_logs, not to job_time_entries; nothing in the clock flow inserts job_time_entries, and the payroll code notes the table has zero rows. So nobody can appear as clocked in here. I found no read of active_clock_sessions in the team routes (grep).
The route's own comment says it errored on a nonexistent column 'since launch' until a fix; the underlying data source is still the wrong table.
Status 'broken' is inferred from code and comments, not verified against the live database.
rebuild: A live board driven by open punches (and location pings where consented): on the clock now, where, since when, and who has not clocked in by their scheduled start.
add: Not clocked in by scheduled start alert
nationwide: Role pair admin and tech_support fixed.

name: Team member day drill-down
purpose: What one person is doing today: clock state, minutes worked, miles, stops, pings, captures, receipts, and a message box.

elements.name: Stats bar
elements.does: Minutes worked, miles, stops, pings, captures, receipts.

elements.name: Active clock-in card
elements.does: Job and duration when present.

elements.name: Quick actions
elements.does: Send ping, open mileage, timeline, captures.

behaviours: One round trip to the today route (592 lines) that joins many tables.
problems: Minutes worked and active clock come from job_time_entries, which is not written by the clock (see people.field-team-tab).
/admin/team (list) redirects away but this detail route stays alone.
rebuild: Make this the 'Today' tab of the single person record.
nationwide: Location data needs per-state employee-monitoring consent; not modelled.

name: Job time entries (second, unused timer table)
purpose: Per-job time rows with start, end, duration, billable flag, vehicle and driver flag, entered from the job page and used for job cost and mileage.

elements.name: Add time entry (job page)
elements.does: POST with work_type, duration_minutes, description; start_time is 'now'.

elements.name: job_time_entries
elements.does: start_time, end_time, duration_minutes, billable, vehicle_id, is_driver.

behaviours: Reports, mileage and job totals read this table.
Payroll notes the table has zero rows and was abandoned as the source for pay.
problems: Second record of hours with a different shape: job reports and mileage read job_time_entries while pay reads daily_time_logs, so a job's labour cost and the payroll hours can disagree.
POST and DELETE only require sign-in: any user can add or delete any job's time rows (no role or ownership check in the route).
Entry always starts 'now' with a typed duration, so start/end are not real.
rebuild: One time record. Job cost, mileage attribution and payroll all read the same punch/timesheet lines (with job, task, vehicle, driver, billable as fields).
add: Billable versus non-billable by job phase
Vehicle and driver on the punch for mileage reimbursement
nationwide: None specific.

name: Still-clocked-in evening reminder
purpose: Nudges anyone still on the clock after 6pm so a forgotten clock-out does not create fake hours.

elements.name: Time test
elements.does: Only after 18:00 in America/Chicago.

elements.name: De-dupe
elements.does: One nag per roughly 6 hours.

behaviours: Reads active_clock_sessions; sends notify() bell/push; does not auto clock-out.
problems: Hard-coded timezone and 6pm for every firm and every shift pattern.
Reminder only; no auto-close rule such as 'close at 14h and flag'.
rebuild: Per-firm and per-person policy: reminder time, auto-close after N hours with a 'needs review' flag.
nationwide: BUSINESS_TZ = America/Chicago is a Starr and Texas constant; needs per-firm timezone.

name: Hours notifications
purpose: Approvers hear when hours are submitted; employees hear when hours are approved, rejected (with reason), adjusted, or entered for them.

elements.name: Per-approver opt-out
elements.does: hours_notification_preferences (seed 579).

behaviours: Recipients are everyone whose roles satisfy canDecideHours (admin).
Deep link opens the approver's queue on that person.
problems: Four people hold admin at Starr, so all are notified unless they opt out; there is no 'my crew only' routing.
rebuild: Route to the person's approver (crew lead, then office) rather than to every admin.
add: Digest instead of one bell per submission
nationwide: Email/push templates carry Starr names.

name: Overtime calculation
purpose: Pay hours over a weekly threshold at a premium.

elements.name: overtime_threshold_weekly
elements.does: Config value, 40.

elements.name: overtime_multiplier
elements.does: Config value, 1.5.

elements.name: Regular-rate method
elements.does: Mixed rates: premium is 0.5 x (straight-time pay / total hours) x OT hours (FLSA style).

behaviours: Computed only when the legacy payroll_runs engine builds a pay stub.
The live path (owed balance, payout batches) sums approved dollars with no overtime step (grep of lib/payroll/owed.ts, lib/payouts, app/api/admin/payouts finds none).
problems: The engine the plans chose to keep (payout_batches) does not compute overtime; the engine that does (payroll_runs) is the one being retired. If the legacy engine is made read-only as decided, overtime disappears from pay.
Weekly 40 only: no daily overtime (CA, AK, NV, CO), no double time, no 7th-day rule, no state or local variants, no exempt/non-exempt flag.
A page text (pay-progression) tells employees overtime is 1.5x the effective rate while the stub code uses a half-time premium on the regular rate: different statements of one rule.
rebuild: A pure, versioned rules module: input = a person's punches for the pay period plus work state and classification; output = hours split regular, OT, DT, PTO, with the rule used named. Rules are data per jurisdiction (federal weekly 40; CA daily 8/12 and 7th day; others). Runs at period close, before the payout batch is built.
add: Exempt vs non-exempt flag with salary threshold
nationwide: Texas follows federal weekly rules. Starr has no daily-OT logic. Every other state rule is missing.

name: Pay model: base pay, activity rates, overrides
purpose: One rule set that prices an hour: a person's base pay, flat activity rates (driving 15) that replace base, and a manual override by whoever pays.

elements.name: Rates tab
elements.does: Edit what each job title or activity is paid.

elements.name: Sentinels
elements.does: 'unspecified' falls to base pay; 'unpriced' means no rate attached.

behaviours: Pure and tested; hours picker, approvals and payroll call the same function.
problems: Rates tab hint says 'what each job title is paid' while the model says base pay is per person: wording and model disagree.
Rate is per person with no effective-dated history in the pricing path (salary history table exists separately).
Pay stamped at submit can go stale if base pay changes later.
rebuild: Keep the three-rule model. Add effective dates and salary vs hourly vs piece/day rate types, priced at period close not at submit.
nationwide: Activity names (driving, drawing, field) are Starr data in seeds.

elements.name: You-are-here hero

elements.name: Edit mode

elements.name: Calculator

elements.name: Override panel
elements.does: user_pay_overrides per employee.

elements.name: Credential queue

behaviours: The owner parked this on 2026-08-04: nothing in the live pay path reads tiers, seniority, credentials or XP.
problems: About 3,200 lines of UI plus eight API routes for a system that does not affect pay today; employees can read an 'effective rate' the payroll never uses (confusing, and a wage-expectation risk).
Key mapping bug history: survey_technician vs survey_tech tiers.
rebuild: Hide until wanted. When wanted, rebuild as 'pay steps': a step table per job title with effective dates; credentials as an optional bonus line. Keep effective-rate.ts and its tests.
add: Raise history and scheduled raises (payroll/raises exists)

elements.name: My pay
elements.does: Personal.

elements.does: Legacy runs and pay-owed.

elements.name: Payouts
elements.does: Ledger of every payout.

elements.name: Payout runs
elements.does: Batches.

elements.name: Withdrawals
elements.does: Queue (admin, finance).

elements.name: Pay changes
elements.does: Rate-change log.

elements.name: Rates
elements.does: Pay rates.

elements.name: Rewards, Manage rewards, How rewards work
elements.does: XP store.

behaviours: Old routes /admin/payroll, /admin/payouts, /admin/payouts/runs, /admin/payouts/withdrawals, /admin/pay-rates, /admin/payout-log, /admin/my-pay, /admin/rewards* redirect here.
Payouts settings, ad-hoc, search, checks and the batch detail pages are NOT tabs; they are still separate routes reached by links.

add: Year-to-date and tax-year summary for employees
nationwide: Withdrawal and finance role names fixed; bank (PNC) and Venmo/Cash App bias.

name: My pay (employee view of money)
purpose: What I am owed, what I have been paid, my balance, my advances, and how I want to be paid.

elements.name: Balance card
elements.does: Available balance and withdrawal request.

No pay statement or YTD, which several states require employees to receive.

purpose: Build a payroll run for a date range: a stub per person with regular and overtime hours, estimated deductions and net, and credit to the balance on completion.

elements.name: Pay stub view
elements.does: Regular hours, OT hours and rate, gross, estimated federal 12%, SS 6.2%, Medicare 1.45%.

elements.does: Preview then create a payout batch (the live engine) from this tab.

elements.name: Employee detail
elements.does: Per-person payroll page.

behaviours: Only approved hours are paid.
On completion credits employee_profiles.available_balance (one of two balance writers).
The plan decided payroll_runs becomes read-only history.
problems: Two engines can pay the same hours; only a date-overlap check (engine-overlap.ts) prevents a double payment, and the payment has no link to time-log ids on the stub side.
Deductions are flat estimates (12/6.2/1.45%, state 0). Printing invented tax figures on a wage statement is the reason S9b/S9c are parked for an accountant.
